title: An opaque handle API
description:
Design a small C interface that hides a C++ class behind a handle.

```
Counter* c = counter_create(10);
counter_add(c, 5);   -> 15
counter_value(c)     -> 15
counter_destroy(c);
counter_add(NULL, 1) -> error code
```
hints: The caller only ever sees `Counter*`; it cannot read the members, so you can change them without breaking it (lesson 3.01).
`counter_create` does `return new (std::nothrow) Counter{start, {}};` so allocation failure returns `nullptr` instead of throwing.
requirements: `typedef struct Counter Counter;` with `create`, `add`, `value` and `destroy`, all `extern "C"`.
Only plain C types cross the interface; a `NULL` handle gives an error code.
Inside, `Counter` is a C++ struct with a `std::vector<int>` history.
stretch: Return results through out-parameters and use the return value only for error codes.
